propositions: The review-bot receiver logs the webhook authentication token in plaintext on every /webhook and /rerun request because uvicorn's default access log records the full request line including query string parameters.
The webhook token is identical to GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN, a Gerrit credential, making the logged secret exploitable for both driving reviews and impersonating the bot against Gerrit.
The exposure is fail-open with no error signal, allowing the secret to persist in journald and any downstream systems that consume journal content without alerting operators to the leak.

The fix moves token authentication from query string (token=...) to X-Rebar-Token HTTP header for both endpoints, and installs a TokenRedactingFilter as a backstop to scrub any token values from access logs before they reach journald.

The previously logged token must be rotated and the rotation recorded separately and explicitly, since fixing the code alone does not un-leak what is already persisted in journald and shared log excerpts.
